record.original_question: Let K be an adequate Smyth category. If X is a K-determined T0 space, is its Smyth power space PS(X) again K-determined?

evidence.quote: Question 7.20. ([49]) Let K be an adequate Smyth category. Is the Smyth power space PS(X) of a K-determined T0 space X again K-determined?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions.

All spaces below are $T_0$ topological spaces. For a $T_0$ space $X$, the specialization order is defined by $x \le y$ iff $x \in \overline{\{y\}}$. A subset $A \subseteq X$ is saturated if $A$ equals the intersection of its open neighborhoods (equivalently, $A$ is an upper set in the specialization order). Let $K(X)$ denote the set of nonempty compact saturated subsets of $X$. The Smyth power space $P_S(X)$ is the set $K(X)$ equipped with the upper Vietoris topology, generated by the basic open sets
$$\Box U = \{ Q \in K(X) : Q \subseteq U \}, \qquad U \subseteq X \text{ open}.$$

A class $\mathcal{K}$ of $T_0$ spaces is called a Smyth category if it is closed under homeomorphisms and is closed under the formation of Smyth power spaces, i.e. $X \in \mathcal{K}$ implies $P_S(X) \in \mathcal{K}$. A Smyth category $\mathcal{K}$ is called adequate if, in addition, for every $T_0$ space $X$ that lies in $\mathcal{K}$, every closed subspace of $X$ also lies in $\mathcal{K}$ and the canonical $T_0$ reflection maps and the Smyth power-space construction interact suitably with $\mathcal{K}$ (in particular, $\mathcal{K}$ contains all sober spaces and is closed under arbitrary topological products and under taking suprema of closed subsets).

For a class $\mathcal{K}$ of $T_0$ spaces, a $T_0$ space $X$ is called $\mathcal{K}$-determined if for every continuous map $f \colon X \to Y$ into a member $Y \in \mathcal{K}$, there is a unique extension to a continuous map from the $\mathcal{K}$-reflection (the free $\mathcal{K}$-space generated by $X$) into $Y$; equivalently, $X$ has the same continuous-map behaviour towards spaces in $\mathcal{K}$ as its $\mathcal{K}$-reflection.

Question. Let $\mathcal{K}$ be an adequate Smyth category, and let $X$ be a $\mathcal{K}$-determined $T_0$ space. Is the Smyth power space $P_S(X)$ also $\mathcal{K}$-determined?
artifact.category_tag: non-Hausdorff topology and Smyth power spaces
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2022–2025) on Smyth power spaces, well-filtered determined spaces, and related Q*-determined spaces continues to investigate when properties pass from a $T_0$ space $X$ to its Smyth power space $P_S(X)$, but no source found in the search explicitly resolves the general question for an arbitrary adequate Smyth category $\mathcal{K}$. The status appears to be unverified in the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Spaces Determined by their Smyth Hyperspaces with the Scott Topology (Order, 2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces Q*-determined spaces and studies their Smyth hyperspaces with the Scott topology.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies determinedness conditions related to the Smyth power construction, but does not appear to settle the general adequate-Smyth-category version.

status_evidence.title: Power structures of directed spaces (arXiv:2204.09926)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies power constructions including Smyth power spaces in categories of directed spaces.
status_evidence.claim: General question of preservation of K-determinedness under P_S for an adequate Smyth category K is not explicitly resolved in retrieved sources.

status_evidence.title: On T0 spaces determined by well-filtered spaces (arXiv:1909.09303)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops the theory of K-determined T0 spaces for various classes K.
status_evidence.claim: Provides framework but the question for general adequate Smyth categories remains stated as an open question in the literature.
